traps.title: The repo is not the store
traps.text: 794 manifests in CI-Marketplace are dev_only or unavailable and never reach hub.ci.computer. A repo grep finds apps (Actual Budget, Baby Buddy, MotionEye, openHAB, Wger, Kavita, Ente, Lychee, Dolibarr, ERPNext) a customer cannot install. The live store has 579.

traps.title: Two apps with the same name
traps.text: Firefly III (firefly-iii vs fireflyiii), Agent Zero (agentzero vs agent-zero), Fish Speech (CUDA vs CPU), Hunyuan3D (CUDA vs ROCm), Trilium (two), InfluxDB (1.x vs 2.x), ONLYOFFICE (four), Stable Diffusion (three), Gitea (plus Gitea Mirror). Persona decision 2026-10-15: name ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors (id onlyoffice), the standalone suite. Document Server is the editing engine and Workspace is a portal that needs it; neither is the persona app.

traps.title: Hermes and OpenClaw each have two listings
traps.text: First-party: ci-hermes ("Hermes", Nous Research build, messaging gateway) and ci-openclaw ("OpenClaw WebCLI", sandboxed, QR pairing, Memory-wired). Third-party: hermes-agent ("Hermes Agent") and openclaw ("OpenClaw", an Umbrel package, messaging control plane). The Alternatives page lists the generic openclaw as the ChatGPT and Claude replacement. Stories and any on-screen store row should use the first-party pair.

traps.title: CUDA is not ROCm
traps.text: Eleven GPU apps need NVIDIA CUDA and will not run on a Core (AMD Ryzen AI Max). Only ComfyUI and Hunyuan3D ROCm declare ROCm. Image generation is covered; AI music (ACE-Step), voice cloning (CosyVoice, Fish Speech), talking-head video, and LLM OCR (olmOCR, DeepSeek OCR) are NOT. Say nothing about speed; the sheet has no image-generation number.

traps.title: Looks local, is not
traps.text: Lingva Translate scrapes Google Translate. SearXNG queries other search engines. PDFMathTranslate defaults to Google or Bing. Music Assistant pulls Spotify and Qobuz. Plex and Emby are closed-source and account-based. Karakeep, Taxhacker, Open Notebook, Sure and Securo can call OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Pluggy or Enable Banking if you give them keys. SafeOS opens its Guardian page from safeos.sh. Firefly III bank import uses GoCardless or Spectre.

traps.title: Needs the outside world to reach the Core
traps.text: Public websites (Ghost, WordPress, Halo), booking pages (Cal.diy), polls (Rallly), live chat (Chatwoot, Papercups), forms (OpnForm, Formbricks), web analytics, a shop (Medusa, PrestaShop), a mail server (Mailu, Stalwart), a live stream (Owncast) and remote camera viewing all need inbound access. The sheet says remote access is not finalised. The founder letter mentions 3 free and 10 Hub Pro tunnels (not on the sheet). Keep these stories on the home LAN, or flag them.

traps.title: Listed is not tested
traps.text: Of the 216 apps in this catalog, 49 have no QA screenshot and 11 say in their own notes they were not boot-tested on a live Hub device (MediKeep, SparkyFitness, Surmai, PS5-MQTT, ebusd, Paperless-GPT, Zerobyte, OpenReader, DVinyl, Snipe-IT, osTicket). Across the whole live store 275 of 579 have no screenshot (e2e/screenshots on origin/main e9477219). The sheet bans simulated capability.

traps.title: Import Tools is gone as an app
traps.text: The sheet and COPY.md still list "Import Tools" as a first-party Hub app. The docs say the standalone app was retired and its catalog listing removed on 2026-08-17; import now ships inside Companion Memory (84 services, opt-in, revocable). There is no manifest to cite. Say Companion Memory imports.

traps.title: Companion Capture is not in the store
traps.text: ci-capture is dev_only. Companion Camera and Saved Searches are Companion Memory features on the sheet, not apps.

traps.title: Manifest text that must not be repeated
traps.text: Plausible: "fully compliant with GDPR, CCPA and PECR". Documenso: "legally-binding electronic signatures". Medikeep: Apple Health and MyChart replacement (no medical claims). Home Assistant "without relying on the cloud" is fine, but its energy features are not described in the manifest. Hermes and OpenClaw manifests say "assistant"; the voice rule says agent.

traps.title: Store rows with no manifest
traps.text: file-browser and runtipi appear in the live store but have no manifest in either local clone or on origin/main. The Alternatives table row "Filebrowser" is ambiguous between file-browser and filebrowser-quantum. Do not name either.

traps.title: Home Assistant is not a Zigbee hub out of the box
traps.text: The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts; integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access are not enabled by default. A story that plugs in a Zigbee stick is not what the listing ships. Network-based devices, the TV and cameras are fine.

traps.title: DoorDash MCP is not dinner
traps.text: It is the DoorDash Drive API for businesses running deliveries and needs developer credentials.

traps.title: Remote access wording
traps.text: OpenClaw and Hermes phone use away from home goes through Hub Private VPN (Tailscale) or Web exposure (Cloudflare) per the docs. The sheet says anywhere access is not finalised. Do not write "from anywhere".

traps.title: The sheet bans a person as a customer
traps.text: COPY.md section 11: "Any person presented as a customer or team member" must not appear. The fictional families are labelled fiction, but the owner should sign off that this does not breach the rule.

traps.title: Third-party names in text only
traps.text: The sheet: third-party software is named in text and never shown as a logo. The CI-Common assets/apps/store folder carries three third-party logos that its own SOURCE.md calls not cleared as standalone brand assets. Do not use app logos in the site or the films.

traps.title: Steam Headless: listed, Valve account, no performance claim
traps.text: Steam Headless is in the live store and on main, and the gamer persona uses it. It runs Steam on the Core and shows the desktop in a browser. Steam needs a Valve account and the library is Valve's, so never write "no account" or "no cloud". The listing asks for GPU passthrough and the package declares no GPU, so a Core may not run a given game well: no frame rate, resolution, latency, "smooth", "gaming PC", "console replacement" or game titles. The container is privileged, so not "sandboxed". Keep the stream on the home network. EmulatorJS and RomM stay out (ROM files); Sunshine is not in the store.

traps.title: Local coding agent versus cloud model keys
traps.text: Code Server, Forgejo, Gitea and JupyterLab ask for no cloud key; the code lives on the Core. A coding agent is private only when it uses the Core's local model. OpenCode and Aider are wired to the Hub's local model by default and can be pointed at cloud providers; say "the model on your Core" and never mention a key. OpenClaw also receives any cloud provider keys the household saved in Hub, Settings, AI. Code Server extensions (and a coding agent extension) can reach outside services. Claude Code is dev_only on main (it lingers in the live store) and needs an Anthropic key: never name it. No parity with a hosted coding model, no tokens-per-second.
